addressed_weaknesses: W1 (no human validation): not addressable without new work. Stated where the reader meets the first result (opening of Sec. 4), in the abstract, Introduction scope sentence, Limitation (i) and the Conclusion; no softening.

W2 (single model): not addressable without new work. Stated at the start of Sec. 4, Limitation (i) now says whether strategies stay close for other models is unknown; headline scoped to one model in abstract, Intro, Discussion, Conclusion.

W3 (access result expected; asymmetric arms): addressed in framing. Abstract, Intro bold finding, Related Work (Westergaard/Cohen) and Sec. 4.1 now say the direction is expected because curators wrote from full papers and that the contribution is the within-paper size plus attribution of missed facts. Asymmetry kept and sharpened: full-text coverage before repair was not scored; added main-run context (17 of 9,371 direct-reading claims unsupported before repair, 0 contradicted; pooled over 93 entries, not the 46-entry subset). Limitation (ix).

W4 (regime compresses differences): addressed. Headline scoped to 2-12 references, 19% full text, inputs within one prompt, one model in abstract, Intro, Discussion and Conclusion; each says the strategies separate where more full text is readable; Sec. 4.3 retitled.

W5 (cued recall): partly. No new analysis; Sec. 4.1 now states that the share of abstract-only facts conveyed that is actually stated in the abstract was not measured (40.1% pooled coverage) and that the memory-only control does not bound cued recall; Limitation (iv).

W6 (no development set): partly. Limitation kept; Sec. 4.2 and Limitation (vi) add that the 20 compared June-November 2026 entries reproduce the ordering and closeness (all within 2.8 points of direct reading's 52.2%), and that the agentic curator's interval excludes zero there (-1.1, -1.8 to -0.3). No claim about how that set was used in development.
W7 (planted-error test lacks controls): not addressable without new work; wording changed to 'false-flag rate was not measured' in abstract, Sec. 4.4 and Limitation (ix).
W8 (narrow reference; extra content unmeasured): partly. Limitation (ii) now adds that draft content beyond the reference is checked only by the audit.

W9 (novelty / generalisable lesson): addressed in framing. Novelty claim rewritten (citation check 2b): cited RAG/LC/GraphRAG comparisons are acknowledged as controlled; difference stated as task, fixed reference list, curator per-paper reference, paradigms under one audit/scoring, measured/manipulated access. Contribution (6) and a 'Measurement lessons' paragraph in the Discussion add the four lessons (asymmetric completion 2.1-point artefact; per-draft vs fixed fact lists; replicate noise as large as reading-strategy differences; matched ablation).

W10 (presentation): addressed. (a) New Appendix A Table (tab:app_experiments) with every experiment, entry set, n compared and dropout reasons, pointed to at the start of Sec. 4; (b) Table 1 caption fixed (memory-only control audited, not repaired); (c) agentic curator described as interval touching zero with 31/42 counts leaning negative; (d) missing-as-zero intervals described as wide and including zero for all three; (e) number-heavy sentences thinned in Secs. 4.2, 4.3, 4.5-4.7; (f) running header left unchanged (style file).
integrated_answers: Q5 (development): Limitation (vi) and Sec. 4.2 report the 2026 set reproducing ordering/closeness.
Q3 (full-text coverage before repair): stated as not scored; added main-run pooled pre-repair counts as context.
Q4 (cued recall): stated as not measured, with the 40.1% pooled figure.
Q6 (false-flag rate): stated as not measured.
Q8 (regime where strategies differ): Sec. 4.3 and Discussion point to the strata and ablation; larger inputs, other models and supplements stated as untested.

Q10 (why replicate noise is separate): one sentence in Sec. 3.3 - the main comparison is a single run and replicates exist only for 30 entries, so intervals resample entries of that run and replicate noise is reported beside them.

Q11 (reproducing the reference): Reproducibility statement says the reference can be rebuilt from public resources (ClinVar, HPO, MedGen) under rights holders' terms; score files carry fact identifiers and statuses, not wording.
